title: Rationale-Guided Learning for Multimodal Emotion Recognition
abstract: arXiv:2608.10448v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition in conversation (MERC) requires understanding complex interactions between verbal and non-verbal cues. However, most existing approaches fundamentally treat this as a direct input-output (multimodal cues-emotion labels) mapping problem, overlooking the causal reasoning that humans use when interpreting emotions. We propose rationale-guided learning (RGL), a novel framework that transforms MERC into a cognitively-inspired reasoning task. Based on dual-process theory, we decompose emotional reasoning into three facets: Intuitive (immediate perception, System 1), Contextual (situational analysis, System 2), and Integrative (synthesis of both). We leverage an MLLM offline to generate structured rationales, which are encoded as memories to guide model training via aligning internal representations with human-like reasoning patterns. Our final model operates without any MLLM overheads at inference time. Exper

translated_title: 理性引导的多模态情感识别学习
translated_abstract: 对话中的多模态情感识别（MERC）需要理解言语和非言语线索之间的复杂交互。然而，现有大多数方法从根本上将其视为直接的输入-输出（多模态线索-情感标签）映射问题，忽视了人类在解释情感时所使用的因果推理。我们提出了理性引导学习（RGL），一种将MERC转化为认知启发的推理任务的新框架。基于双过程理论，我们将情感推理分解为三个层面：直觉（即时感知，系统1）、情境（情境分析，系统2）和整合（两者综合）。我们利用离线MLLM生成结构化理性，这些理性被编码为记忆，通过将内部表示与类人推理模式对齐来指导模型训练。我们的最终模型在推理时无需任何MLLM开销。实验表明...
tldr: 提出了一种基于双过程理论的理性引导学习框架，通过离线生成结构化理性来指导多模态情感识别模型的训练，在推理时无需额外开销。
en_tdlr: Proposes a rationale-guided learning framework based on dual-process theory, which uses offline-generated structured rationales to guide multimodal emotion recognition model training without any inference-time overhead.
